mission.name: Data Analysis Verification Lab
mission.seoTitle: AI Data Analysis Verification Lab | AhaFrame
mission.description: Verify an AI-generated data analysis by separating extraction, arithmetic, outlier handling, and uncertainty into explicit evidence checks.
mission.hero: The model says Segment B improved operating efficiency the most. The chart looks convincing. One denominator came from the wrong table row. Build a verification policy before accepting the conclusion.
mission.quick: AI data analysis is trustworthy only when extraction, calculation, coverage, outliers, and uncertainty can be verified independently of the model’s prose.

brief.title: The chart can be right-looking and numerically wrong.
brief.role: You are reviewing an AI-generated operating analysis.
brief.body: The source report contains tables, footnotes, percentages, and one malformed value. The AI summary identifies a winning segment, but the derived metric depends on a denominator extracted from the wrong row.
brief.objective: Reduce numerical error risk and make the conclusion reproducible without manually checking every cell.
brief.stakes: A wrong analytical conclusion can redirect budget or strategy even when the narrative is perfectly fluent.

ui.waiting: Inspect the dataset signals, change the verification policy, then rerun the analysis.

debrief.title: Verification should be decomposed the same way the analysis is decomposed.
debrief.rule: Do not ask the model whether its own analysis is correct; create independent checks for extraction, arithmetic, coverage, and interpretation.
debrief.body: AI can accelerate document extraction and exploratory analysis, but it can also silently normalize malformed data, reuse the wrong denominator, or express uncertain interpretation with confident prose. A better workflow uses schema checks for extraction, deterministic recomputation for arithmetic, explicit outlier review, and uncertainty attached to the evidence step that produced it.
points: Separate model interpretation from deterministic arithmetic.
Schema failures should become visible data quality events, not silently repaired text.
Outliers can be parsing errors or the most important signal; do not delete them by default.
Uncertainty is more useful when localized to a step and evidence source.

takeaways: Extraction, calculation and interpretation can fail independently and need different checks.
Derived metrics should be independently reproducible outside the language model.
Attach uncertainty to the row, source or transformation that created it.
